intro: Person-centred care shapes support around the individual's needs, wishes and whole life story, treating them as an equal partner in their care.
points: Always assume an adult has capacity under the Mental Capacity Act; never judge it by age, diagnosis or an unwise choice.
Gain consent every time — spoken or non-verbal — and respect that a person can withdraw it at any point.
If someone genuinely lacks capacity, act in their best interests and choose the least restrictive option.
Person-centred care asks what matters to the person, not just what is the matter, shaping support around them.
Read, follow and help review the care plan; following an out-of-date plan is not person-centred care.
Enable active participation and real choice, protect dignity, and meet holistic physical, emotional, social, cultural and spiritual needs.
